topic: Research: Google ADK vs LangGraph vs CrewAI: Which AI Agent Framework Wins in 2026?
keyword: google adk vs langgraph vs crewai

key_points: In this April 2026 comparison, Afnexis positions ADK for Google-cloud production workflows (including Vertex AI Agent Engine) while LangGraph is preferred for complex branching with explicit state control and LangSmith observability.
The article highlights ADK as model-agnostic through LiteLLM (e.g., Gemini, GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet), with A2A protocol interoperability to call agents from other frameworks.
It frames CrewAI as fastest for demos/prototypes and ADK as faster for production deployment/observability in Google-first stacks.
Q2 2026 report says LangGraph has the largest production deployment footprint, with strong enterprise maturity and orchestration depth.
CrewAI is described as strongest for rapid prototype-to-demo flow, while LangGraph wins for production-level durability and control.
Presenc estimates 2026 production deployment share in Q1: LangGraph ~38%, CrewAI ~12%, Google ADK ~4%.
RaftLabs 2026 view: LangGraph leads for complex stateful workflows, CrewAI for role-based teams, and ADK 2.0 for multi-language enterprise integration.
They explicitly call out AutoGen as having shifted to maintenance mode in 2026 and emphasize framework choice based on production scenario rather than one-size-fits-all performance claims.
The timeline highlights ADK 2.0 reaching production with Python/Go/TypeScript support and Google Cloud-native integration path.
Crewship compares ecosystem signals directly, reporting CrewAI ~45,000 GitHub stars vs LangGraph ~25,500 stars but LangGraph around ~38M monthly PyPI downloads versus ~5M for CrewAI.
It calls out LangGraph’s graph architecture as a control advantage for multi-path workflows despite CrewAI’s faster entry and simpler conventions.
The piece notes LangGraph 1.0 and CrewAI 1.9.x release tracks to show comparable maturity windows in 2026.
The market map emphasizes that GitHub stars can overstate adoption, while LangGraph’s ~34.5M monthly downloads indicate deeper production dependency.
It identifies a strong enterprise-production edge for LangGraph, while CrewAI is framed as a faster prototyping winner.
The article argues interoperability standards (MCP + A2A) are now central, and positions ADK as a key wildcard because of native A2A support.

stats.fact: Google ADK 2.0 GA for Python was announced as of May 19, 2026, introducing graph-based and collaborative workflows.
ADK 2.0 is migrating from hierarchical execution to a graph-based workflow runtime with event schema changes and resumability-focused session data.
ADK 2.0 release notes emphasize event compaction controls and built-in human-in-the-loop confirmation workflows via ToolContext/requestConfirmation(), helping long-running context and safety control.
ADK exposes extensive integrations including LangChain, CrewAI, A2A, and multiple Google services through a broad module surface.
LangGraph interrupt primitives persist graph checkpoints so execution can pause for human approval and resume later using thread-aware persistence.
As of June 11, 2026, GitHub stars were: google/adk-python 20,074; langchain-ai/langgraph 34,456; crewAIInc/crewAI 53,280.

ADK Arena benchmark (arXiv 2606.05548, submitted Jun 4, 2026) reports 51 ADK frameworks across 204 benchmark pairs, generation success 57%, cost range $0.6 to $3.4 per agent (5.6x spread), and median task resolution 32%.

A large-scale 2026 study on multi-agent systems reports over 42K unique commits and over 4.7K resolved issues across eight leading systems, with bugs, infrastructure, and coordination concerns dominant.

angles: Google ADK’s 2.0 architecture marks a shift from prototyping speed toward enterprise runtime rigor with compaction, confirmation hooks, and graph workflows.
The key 2026 battleground is operational maturity: checkpointing, observability, and failure control often outweigh raw feature lists.
Interoperability is becoming a core moat; A2A and MCP allow mixed-framework composition and reduce migration risk.
CrewAI and ADK both move fast for prototypes, but teams may migrate toward LangGraph-like control planes as reliability requirements harden.
Evaluation studies are now large-scale enough to challenge framework hype with concrete cost-success trade-offs and API ergonomics metrics.
